title: Boston Scientific OPAL HDx Electrophysiology Mapping System - Calibration or Quality-Control Test Fails
description: Troubleshoots failed system checks or quality verification by checking setup, accessories, connections, environment, test equipment, and repeatability before escalation.

steps.title: 1. Remove the System From Clinical Dependence
steps.instructions: Do not use a system for patient mapping when a required calibration, quality-control, or verification test has failed. Move the procedure to verified equipment if continued mapping capability is required. Expected outcome: No patient depends on equipment that has not passed required verification.

steps.title: 2. Identify the Exact Failed Test
steps.instructions: Record: Name of the test Exact displayed result or message Stage at which it fails Whether it fails consistently Whether any system component was recently changed Do not assume all failed system checks represent a calibration failure. Expected outcome: The specific verification failure is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify Correct Test Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm the test is being performed using the intended external connections, accessories, and approved test equipment. Check that the test setup matches the applicable manufacturer or facility procedure. Expected outcome: The test configuration is correct and repeatable.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Test Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible connections involved in the test for: Loose connectors Damaged cables Bent contacts Contamination Incorrect connections Strain or intermittent movement Expected outcome: Test connections are secure and intact. If correcting a connection produces a valid passing result, repeat the test to confirm before stopping troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Verify Accessories and Test Equipment
steps.instructions: Confirm external accessories and test equipment being used are appropriate and in suitable condition. If practical, substitute a known-good compatible accessory or test cable. Do not adjust calibration values simply to obtain a passing result. Expected outcome: A defective external accessory or test connection is either ruled out or identified.

steps.title: 6. Check Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Look for environmental factors that may affect testing, including: Equipment movement Electromagnetic interference Unstable external power Improper cable routing Recently added nearby equipment Correct obvious external conditions before repeating the test. Expected outcome: The test environment is stable and appropriate.

steps.title: 7. Restart and Repeat Only Through Approved Procedures
steps.instructions: If permitted, restart the system and repeat the failed test exactly as required by approved documentation. Do not repeatedly recalibrate or change configuration without understanding why the test failed. Expected outcome: The test passes consistently using the proper setup. If it does, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 8. Compare With a Known-Good Setup
steps.instructions: Where possible, compare the test setup, accessories, or external connections with a known-good OPAL HDx configuration. Avoid changing multiple variables simultaneously. Expected outcome: Any external difference contributing to the failure is identified.

steps.title: 9. Escalate a Repeatable Test Failure
steps.instructions: If the calibration or quality-control test continues to fail with correct setup, known-good external accessories, and stable conditions, remove the system from service. Do not bypass the test or record a passing result that was not achieved. Expected outcome: The failed system is escalated for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the OPAL HDx quality-control check would not complete successfully before use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose external test connection causing inconsistent verification results.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, repeated the approved quality check successfully, confirmed repeatability, and returned the system to service.

title: Boston Scientific OPAL HDx Electrophysiology Mapping System - Cooling, Fan, or Overtemperature Fault Occurs
description: Troubleshoots overheating indications, abnormal fan behavior, blocked ventilation, room conditions, equipment placement, and recurring thermal shutdowns before service escalation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Respond to Thermal Warnings
steps.instructions: Do not continue relying on a mapping system that reports overheating, repeatedly shuts down, emits unusual odor, or shows signs of excessive heat. Coordinate with the clinical team and transfer the procedure to verified equipment if continued mapping is required. Expected outcome: The patient no longer depends on equipment with a potentially unsafe thermal condition.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Thermal Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the system: Displays an overtemperature message Has unusually loud fan operation Has no audible fan operation when normally expected Becomes excessively warm externally Shuts down after operating for a period Produces unusual odor or noise If smoke, burning odor, or visible damage is present, disconnect the device from service and do not continue troubleshooting while energized. Expected outcome: The thermal symptom and affected component are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Ventilation Openings
steps.instructions: Check accessible vents for: Dust accumulation Obstruction Equipment pushed against walls or cabinetry Drapes or supplies blocking airflow Cables or objects covering ventilation areas Do not open internal covers simply to clean internal fans. Expected outcome: External ventilation openings are unobstructed. If correcting an airflow obstruction resolves the condition and testing is stable, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Check Equipment Placement
steps.instructions: Verify adequate external clearance around system components according to the installed environment and applicable manufacturer guidance. Look for recently relocated equipment, added carts, or items placed against ventilated surfaces. Expected outcome: Equipment placement permits normal external airflow.

steps.title: 5. Check the Room Environment
steps.instructions: Determine whether the room is unusually warm or whether HVAC performance has changed. Compare conditions with nearby equipment and ask whether other devices have reported temperature problems. Expected outcome: A room-level environmental problem is identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 6. Inspect for Excessive Dust Externally
steps.instructions: Examine accessible vents and filters only where they are intended for routine external service. Clean or replace serviceable external items only according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: Accessible airflow surfaces are reasonably clean and unobstructed.

steps.title: 7. Observe Fan and Thermal Behavior
steps.instructions: With the device out of patient use, operate it under normal conditions and observe whether the reported thermal condition returns. Listen for: Grinding Rattling Fan surging Fan stopping unexpectedly Do not insert tools into fan openings. Expected outcome: Cooling behavior remains stable without recurring thermal messages or abnormal noise.

steps.title: 8. Verify Normal Operation After Cooling
steps.instructions: If the system was allowed to return to a normal temperature, restart it using the approved sequence and perform an operational check. Do not repeatedly restart a system that quickly overheats. Expected outcome: The system starts and remains stable without recurring thermal symptoms. Troubleshooting can stop if the corrected external cause is clear.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Recurring Thermal Faults
steps.instructions: If overheating, abnormal fan behavior, thermal shutdown, or excessive heat recurs after external airflow and room conditions are verified, remove the system from service. Do not perform internal fan, power-supply, or thermal-control repairs without authorized service procedures. Expected outcome: The system is prevented from further clinical use until qualified evaluation is completed.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the OPAL HDx displayed an overtemperature condition after operating in the procedure room.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found supplies positioned against an external ventilation opening and restricting airflow.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleared the obstruction, allowed the system to normalize, and verified stable operation without recurrence of the thermal condition.

title: Boston Scientific OPAL HDx Electrophysiology Mapping System - Detector or Acquisition Hardware Is Not Ready
description: Troubleshoots unavailable mapping or signal-acquisition hardware by checking startup state, external connections, electrodes, cables, accessories, and workstation communication.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Required Monitoring
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot unreliable acquisition hardware while clinical staff depend on it for procedural information. Maintain required ECG, hemodynamic, and other patient monitoring independently and coordinate any catheter or electrode changes with clinical staff. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring and procedural safety are maintained independently of the affected mapping acquisition path.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Hardware Is Not Ready
steps.instructions: Determine what the system reports as unavailable. Identify whether the issue involves: Mapping acquisition Surface ECG connections Catheter connections An external interface module A workstation-to-hardware communication path One accessory versus the entire acquisition system Record any displayed status message exactly. Expected outcome: The unavailable acquisition path is clearly defined.

steps.title: 3. Verify Complete System Startup
steps.instructions: Confirm that all required OPAL HDx system components have completed normal startup. Check for components with no power indication or a workstation that appears ready before associated acquisition hardware has initialized. Expected outcome: Required system components are powered and have completed initialization. If a delayed component becomes ready normally, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Acquisition Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible acquisition-related cables and connectors for: Loose connections Bent or damaged contacts Contamination Improper seating Cable strain Visible cuts or damage Reseat approved external connectors when safe. Expected outcome: Acquisition connections are secure and physically intact. If reseating restores normal hardware recognition, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Patient Interface Accessories
steps.instructions: With clinical involvement as required, inspect external electrodes, leads, catheter interface cables, and other patient-connected accessories relevant to the unavailable acquisition path. Do not manipulate invasive patient connections without the responsible clinical team. Expected outcome: Required accessories are present, compatible, correctly connected, and visibly intact.

steps.title: 6. Substitute a Known-Good External Accessory
steps.instructions: When safe and available, replace a suspect cable or external interface accessory with a compatible known-good item. Change only one item at a time so the cause can be identified. Expected outcome: If the hardware becomes ready with the known-good accessory, the original accessory is isolated as faulty and should be removed from service.

steps.title: 7. Verify Workstation Communication
steps.instructions: Check whether the workstation shows the expected acquisition hardware as connected and available. Inspect external communication connections between system components and confirm no cable was disturbed during setup. Avoid changing network or system configuration values without authorization. Expected outcome: Workstation and acquisition hardware communicate normally.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Nonpatient Acquisition Check
steps.instructions: When permitted and with no patient dependent on the system, perform an approved functional acquisition check using appropriate simulation or test methods available to Clinical Engineering. Expected outcome: The system recognizes acquisition hardware and receives stable expected test inputs. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Hardware-Not-Ready Conditions
steps.instructions: If acquisition hardware remains unavailable after external connections, accessories, startup, and communication paths have been verified, remove the affected system from clinical use. Do not perform internal board-level troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The system is appropriately escalated for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the OPAL HDx acquisition hardware remained unavailable during procedure setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external acquisition interface cable not fully seated.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the cable, verified normal hardware recognition and stable test acquisition, and returned the system to service.

title: Boston Scientific OPAL HDx Electrophysiology Mapping System - DICOM, PACS, or Worklist Transfer Fails
description: Troubleshoots supported networked study, worklist, or export functions by checking network connectivity, destination availability, patient data, configuration, and infrastructure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Separate Clinical Operation From Data Transfer
steps.instructions: Do not interrupt active mapping or patient monitoring solely to troubleshoot a noncritical network transfer unless the failure affects safe clinical operation. Determine whether the study can continue safely while data-transfer troubleshooting is deferred. Expected outcome: Patient care remains uninterrupted while the transfer problem is assessed.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Network Function Actually Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the reported problem involves: Patient or procedure worklist Study transfer Archive or server communication Another supported network export A separate workstation or integration system Confirm that the requested DICOM, PACS, or worklist function is actually configured and supported in the local OPAL HDx installation. Expected outcome: The exact network service and destination are identified.

steps.title: 3. Record the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Capture: Exact message Time of failure Destination involved Whether all studies fail or only one Whether the problem affects all patients Whether transfer previously worked that day Expected outcome: The problem can be correlated with device or infrastructure behavior.

steps.title: 4. Check Physical Network Connectivity
steps.instructions: Inspect the accessible network cable and connection. Check for: Loose cable Damaged latch or connector No link indication where visible Cable disconnected during equipment movement Use a known-good approved network cable when appropriate. Expected outcome: Physical network connectivity is intact. If replacing or reconnecting the cable restores transfer, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Verify Other Network Functions
steps.instructions: Determine whether other supported network functions from the system are working. If every networked function has failed, suspect the local connection or infrastructure before assuming an application-specific problem. Expected outcome: The fault is narrowed to the entire network path or one specific service.

steps.title: 6. Verify Patient and Study Information
steps.instructions: Check that required patient or study fields used by the local workflow are populated correctly. Do not alter clinical identifiers merely to force a transfer. If only one study fails, compare it with a study that transfers normally. Expected outcome: Required data is present and no obvious record-specific issue explains the failure.

steps.title: 7. Check Destination Availability
steps.instructions: Coordinate with PACS, imaging informatics, clinical IT, or the appropriate system owner to determine whether the destination server or worklist service is available. Check whether other devices are experiencing similar failures. Expected outcome: A hospital infrastructure outage is either identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 8. Verify Approved Network Configuration
steps.instructions: Review visible configuration information only if authorized. Compare with documented local configuration rather than changing: Network addressing Destination entries Application endpoints Other integration settings Do not make undocumented configuration changes. Expected outcome: Existing configuration matches the approved site setup or discrepancies are escalated to the appropriate support team.

steps.title: 9. Retry the Transfer and Verify Receipt
steps.instructions: After correcting an external connection or after infrastructure service is restored, retry the affected workflow. Confirm not only that the system reports success but that the intended receiving system actually receives the expected information. Expected outcome: Transfer completes end to end. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Integration Failure
steps.instructions: If local connectivity, patient data, destination availability, and approved configuration appear correct but the transfer still fails, escalate jointly to qualified system support and the appropriate IT or integration team. Expected outcome: The unresolved network or application issue is routed to the correct service owner.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the OPAL HDx could not transfer supported study information to the configured network destination.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the system's external network cable disconnected at the wall connection.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering restored the network connection and verified successful end-to-end transfer and receipt at the configured destination.

title: Boston Scientific OPAL HDx Electrophysiology Mapping System - Exposure or Scan Will Not Start or Is Aborted
description: Troubleshoots mapping-acquisition or associated procedure-start failures by identifying the affected function, readiness state, connections, accessories, and integrated equipment.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Clarify the Failed Function
steps.instructions: Do not repeatedly attempt a failed procedure function while the patient depends on unreliable equipment. OPAL HDx is an electrophysiology mapping system, so first determine whether staff are referring to mapping acquisition or to an exposure or scan performed by separate imaging equipment. Expected outcome: The affected function and responsible asset are identified.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether: Mapping acquisition will not begin Acquisition starts and then stops A separate imaging system will not expose or scan The OPAL HDx loses readiness when acquisition begins A repeatable message appears Record the message and sequence of events. Expected outcome: The exact start or abort condition is reproducible and clearly documented.

steps.title: 3. Verify OPAL HDx Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm the mapping system has completed startup and required acquisition hardware is available. Check for unresolved readiness messages, disconnected accessories, or unavailable inputs before starting a new acquisition. Expected outcome: The OPAL HDx is in its normal ready state before acquisition is attempted.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Acquisition Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible mapping, catheter-interface, ECG, communication, and other relevant external connections. Look for loose or strained connectors, cable damage, or connections disturbed during patient setup. Expected outcome: Required acquisition connections are secure and intact.

steps.title: 5. Verify Required Accessories
steps.instructions: Confirm required patient-interface accessories are properly connected and recognized. Coordinate all invasive or patient-connected changes with clinical personnel. When appropriate, substitute a compatible known-good external cable or accessory. Expected outcome: Required accessories are recognized and stable. If replacement of an accessory restores acquisition, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Controls and Procedure State
steps.instructions: Confirm the system is in the intended clinical operating state using normal controls. Do not enter restricted service menus or alter configuration merely to force acquisition. Check whether the workstation is waiting for an expected clinical selection or whether an interrupted prior workflow remains active. Expected outcome: Normal controls permit acquisition to begin without bypassing system safeguards.

steps.title: 7. Separate Mapping From Imaging Equipment
steps.instructions: If the complaint actually concerns X-ray exposure, fluoroscopy, CT, or another imaging scan, troubleshoot that imaging system separately. Verify whether OPAL HDx remains functional while the other equipment reports the failure. Expected outcome: The problem is correctly isolated to the mapping system or the separate imaging asset.

steps.title: 8. Perform Controlled Functional Verification
steps.instructions: With no patient dependent on the system, verify that an approved test acquisition can begin, remain active, and stop normally. Observe the workstation and acquisition hardware for disconnects or repeated aborts. Expected outcome: Acquisition starts and completes normally without interruption. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Repeated Acquisition Aborts
steps.instructions: If mapping acquisition repeatedly aborts after external connections, accessories, and readiness conditions are verified, remove the system from service and escalate. Expected outcome: An unreliable acquisition system is not returned to clinical use without further evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that mapping acquisition on the OPAL HDx would begin and then immediately stop.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose external acquisition connection that became intermittent when the cable was moved.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, verified stable test acquisition without interruption, and returned the system to service.

title: Boston Scientific OPAL HDx Electrophysiology Mapping System - Gantry, Table, or Positioning Motion Is Unavailable
description: Troubleshoots unavailable positioning or associated table-motion functions by checking safety interlocks, controls, connections, obstructions, and integrated equipment before escalation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient From Unintended Movement
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot unavailable or unpredictable positioning while patient safety depends on the affected motion system. Prevent unintended patient movement, secure lines and catheters, and have clinical staff maintain safe patient positioning. Use alternate positioning methods only when approved for the procedure. Expected outcome: The patient is secure and no troubleshooting action can produce unsafe motion.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Motion Function Is Affected
steps.instructions: Determine exactly what clinical staff mean by unavailable motion. Identify whether the problem involves: An associated procedure table An integrated positioning device A peripheral navigation component One direction of movement All movement A control input that is not responding Do not assume the OPAL HDx itself contains a gantry or powered patient table. Expected outcome: The affected external or integrated positioning component is identified. If the reported function belongs to another asset, route troubleshooting to that equipment.

steps.title: 3. Verify Power to the Affected Positioning Equipment
steps.instructions: Confirm that the table or positioning component has facility power and shows normal power indications. Check accessible power cords, plugs, approved power distribution, and emergency-stop conditions where applicable. Do not bypass interlocks or emergency-stop circuits. Expected outcome: The affected component has normal power available. If power restoration returns normal motion, troubleshooting can stop after controlled verification.

steps.title: 4. Check for Mechanical Obstruction
steps.instructions: Inspect the immediate area for: Equipment blocking movement Cables caught under wheels or moving sections Patient lines limiting travel Accessories interfering with movement Locked casters or transport features Physical contact with another system Do not force movement against resistance. Expected outcome: The intended motion path is clear and no external obstruction is present. If removal of an obstruction restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop after testing.

steps.title: 5. Inspect External Control Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible connections for foot controls, hand controls, interface cables, or other external positioning controls associated with the affected equipment. Look for disconnected, loose, damaged, or contaminated connectors. Expected outcome: External positioning controls and connections are intact and securely connected.

steps.title: 6. Verify Control State and Interlocks
steps.instructions: Confirm that normal clinical control conditions are satisfied according to approved operating procedures. Check for obvious: Emergency-stop activation Transport or lock mode Incomplete system startup Accessory not fully seated Another control station holding priority Do not bypass safety interlocks. Expected outcome: No external control-state condition is preventing authorized motion.

steps.title: 7. Isolate the Mapping System From the Positioning Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether OPAL HDx remains operational while only the associated positioning device is unavailable. If the table or motion device is a separate asset, test it independently using its approved troubleshooting process. Expected outcome: The fault is isolated to either the mapping system interface or the separate positioning equipment.

steps.title: 8. Perform Controlled Motion Verification
steps.instructions: With no risk to a patient, test available positioning functions using normal controls. Observe for: Smooth response Correct direction No unexpected stops No unusual noise No intermittent control response Expected outcome: Required positioning functions operate consistently. Troubleshooting can stop if normal controlled operation is restored.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Unresolved or Unsafe Motion Problems
steps.instructions: If motion remains unavailable, intermittent, or unpredictable, remove the affected positioning equipment from service. Do not perform internal motor, drive, control-board, or interlock repair without approved service procedures. Expected outcome: Unsafe or unresolved positioning equipment is prevented from clinical use and referred for qualified repair.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the procedure table would not move while preparing the OPAL HDx setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external equipment cable obstructing the table's travel path and preventing normal positioning.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleared and secured the cable, verified smooth table movement in the required directions, and confirmed the mapping-system setup remained operational.

helpfulDetails: Separate table or positioning asset involved

title: Boston Scientific OPAL HDx Electrophysiology Mapping System - Image Quality Is Poor or Artifacts Are Present
description: Troubleshoots poor mapping display quality, unstable signals, or artifacts caused by electrodes, cables, positioning, interference, connections, or acquisition conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Do Not Rely on Questionable Data
steps.instructions: Do not allow clinical decisions to depend on mapping or displayed information known to be unreliable. Maintain independent patient monitoring and notify the clinical team that the mapping information may be affected. Expected outcome: Patient care does not depend solely on questionable mapping or signal information.

steps.title: 2. Define the Artifact
steps.instructions: Determine whether the complaint involves: Noisy intracardiac signals Unstable surface ECG Intermittent signal loss Distorted mapping information Display artifacts A problem seen only with one catheter or channel A problem affecting all acquisition Ask whether the issue changes when equipment, cables, or the patient moves. Expected outcome: The artifact pattern and affected signal path are identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Patient Electrodes and External Leads
steps.instructions: With clinical staff, verify surface electrodes and external patient leads are correctly applied, secure, and undamaged. Poor contact, loose electrodes, dried conductive surfaces, and cable movement can create significant artifact. Expected outcome: Patient electrodes and external leads provide secure, stable connections. If correcting an electrode resolves the artifact, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Catheter and Acquisition Cables
steps.instructions: Check accessible catheter interface and acquisition cables for: Loose connectors Bent or damaged contacts Cable strain Cuts or insulation damage Connections sensitive to movement Do not manipulate invasive devices without appropriate clinical involvement. Expected outcome: External acquisition cables are secure and physically intact.

steps.title: 5. Isolate the Problem Using Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: When clinically appropriate, substitute a compatible known-good cable, lead, or external accessory. Change one item at a time. Expected outcome: If the artifact disappears with a known-good accessory, the original accessory is isolated and removed from service.

steps.title: 6. Check Cable Routing and Environmental Interference
steps.instructions: Inspect whether signal cables are bundled with power cords, lying across high-interference equipment, under tension, or routed differently than during normal operation. Look for recently added powered equipment near the procedure area. Reposition external cables without compromising patient safety or sterile fields. Expected outcome: Cable routing and environmental conditions do not introduce obvious interference.

steps.title: 7. Verify System and Signal Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm staff are using the intended clinical configuration and display settings for the procedure. Do not make undocumented configuration changes or enter unauthorized service menus. Compare the current setup with a known normal setup when available. Expected outcome: The observed artifact is not caused by an unintended external setting or configuration selection.

steps.title: 8. Determine Whether the Problem Is Mapping Data or the Display
steps.instructions: If possible, compare signals across available displays or outputs. Check whether the underlying acquired signal is abnormal or whether only one display device shows visual distortion. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to the signal/acquisition path or to an external display component.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using an approved test method when appropriate, confirm stable signal acquisition without unexplained noise, dropout, or visual artifact. Expected outcome: Signal quality remains stable during observation and normal cable movement. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Signal or Mapping Artifacts
steps.instructions: If artifacts remain after electrodes, cables, accessories, routing, displays, and settings are verified, remove the system from service if reliable mapping cannot be assured. Expected outcome: Unreliable mapping data is not returned to clinical use without qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported intermittent noise and artifact on the OPAL HDx mapping signals during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering isolated the artifact to a damaged external acquisition cable that produced noise when flexed.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the cable with a known-good compatible cable and verified stable signal acquisition without recurrent artifact.

title: Boston Scientific OPAL HDx Electrophysiology Mapping System - Study Will Not Save, Reconstruct, or Export
description: Troubleshoots study-save, processing, or export failures involving workflow state, storage, patient data, network destinations, external media, and workstation stability.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Existing Data
steps.instructions: Do not immediately restart, power-cycle, or disconnect the workstation if unsaved procedure data may still be recoverable. Coordinate with the clinical team and preserve the current study state whenever possible. Expected outcome: Available clinical data is protected while the failure is investigated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Function Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the system cannot: Save the active study Reopen or process saved data Complete a reconstruction or processing step Export the study Send information to a configured destination Access previously stored studies Record the exact message and workflow step. Expected outcome: The failed function and affected study are identified.

steps.title: 3. Determine Whether the Problem Affects One Study or All Studies
steps.instructions: Check whether the failure: Occurs only with the current study Affects multiple studies Began after a workstation freeze Appears only when exporting Appears only with one destination Do not create unnecessary test patient records in a production system. Expected outcome: The issue is narrowed to a single study, application workflow, storage function, or external destination.

steps.title: 4. Verify Required Study Information
steps.instructions: Confirm that necessary patient and study information has been entered correctly for the local workflow. Do not alter patient identifiers simply to force a save or export. Expected outcome: Required study information is present and consistent.

steps.title: 5. Check Workstation Responsiveness
steps.instructions: Verify the workstation remains responsive and that normal controls operate. If the system is freezing or severely delayed, avoid repeated save commands that may create additional uncertainty. Expected outcome: Workstation stability is confirmed or identified as part of the problem.

steps.title: 6. Check External Network or Destination Connections
steps.instructions: If saving locally works but export fails, inspect the external network connection and determine whether the configured receiving destination is available. Coordinate with IT or the system owner if a server, archive, or integration endpoint may be unavailable. Expected outcome: Local study processing is separated from network or destination failure.

steps.title: 7. Check Approved External Media When Used
steps.instructions: If an approved external export device or removable medium is part of the workflow, verify it is: Properly connected Recognized by the system Appropriate for the intended workflow Not visibly damaged Do not connect unauthorized media to a clinical system. Expected outcome: The external export path is available or isolated as the cause.

steps.title: 8. Avoid Unapproved File Manipulation
steps.instructions: Do not manually delete system files, alter database content, modify operating-system storage, or use unsupported utilities to free space or recover a study. If the system reports a storage-related problem that cannot be corrected through approved user-accessible functions, escalate. Expected outcome: Study integrity is protected and unsupported actions are avoided.

steps.title: 9. Retry the Workflow After Correcting the External Cause
steps.instructions: After restoring a network connection, destination, approved media, or other external dependency, retry the affected save or export operation. Verify the study is actually present at the intended destination. Expected outcome: Study processing completes and the data is accessible where expected. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: With no patient dependent on the system, verify an approved test workflow can: Create or access a study as appropriate Perform required processing Save normally Export through the intended supported path Expected outcome: Study handling functions operate consistently without freezes or errors.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Persistent Study-Handling Failures
steps.instructions: If the study cannot be saved, processed, reconstructed, or exported after external workflow, network, and destination causes are ruled out, remove the system from service when the failure compromises clinical operation or data integrity. Do not perform unsupported database or operating-system repair. Expected outcome: The system and any affected clinical data are referred for qualified support without additional risk to study integrity.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that an OPAL HDx study saved locally but would not export to the configured network destination.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the workstation's external network connection had been disconnected.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering restored the network connection, repeated the export, verified receipt at the configured destination, and confirmed normal study handling.

helpfulDetails: Exact save, processing, or export failure

title: Boston Scientific OPAL HDx Electrophysiology Mapping System - System Will Not Power On or Complete Startup
description: Troubleshoots no-power, incomplete startup, peripheral initialization, external power, connection, workstation, and accessory conditions before service-level evaluation.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Procedure Continuity
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable mapping system while a patient or active electrophysiology procedure depends on it. Notify the clinical team and maintain required monitoring using verified alternate equipment. If the failure occurs during a case, preserve patient safety and procedural data before restarting or disconnecting equipment whenever clinically appropriate. Expected outcome: The patient is supported independently of the affected mapping system and troubleshooting can proceed safely.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the system: Has no signs of power Powers partially but does not complete startup Stops at a particular startup screen Starts the workstation but not associated mapping hardware Displays a repeatable message Restarts unexpectedly Record any displayed message exactly rather than interpreting it. Expected outcome: The failure point is clearly identified. If the system subsequently completes startup normally and remains stable, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 3. Verify Facility Power
steps.instructions: Inspect the power path from the system to the facility source. Verify: Power cords are fully seated Plugs, connectors, and receptacles show no damage Required power distribution components are switched on The outlet is functional using an approved method No circuit protection or facility-power condition is evident Do not bypass grounding, protective devices, or approved power distribution. Expected outcome: Reliable facility power is confirmed at the equipment. If restoring the power connection corrects startup and repeated startup testing passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External System Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible connections between the workstation, display equipment, acquisition/mapping hardware, interface units, and other system components. Look for: Loose connectors Partially seated cables Bent or damaged connector hardware Cables under tension Recently disconnected components Connections disturbed during room cleaning or equipment movement Reseat only user-accessible or Clinical Engineering-approved external connections. Expected outcome: All required external connections are secure and undamaged. If startup completes normally after correcting a connection, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Check Displays and External Peripherals
steps.instructions: Verify monitors and required external peripherals have power and are correctly connected. A powered system with a blank display can be mistaken for a startup failure. Check for indicator lights, display input selection, and obvious peripheral power issues. Expected outcome: Required displays and peripherals operate normally. If the apparent startup problem was isolated to a peripheral, correct or replace that peripheral and verify complete system operation.

steps.title: 6. Remove Nonessential External Accessories When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If safe and permitted, disconnect recently added or nonessential external accessories that could interfere with initialization. Do not disconnect required patient interfaces during patient use. Restart only in accordance with approved operating procedures. Expected outcome: The system completes startup with required hardware connected. If one external accessory consistently causes the failure, remove that accessory from use and troubleshooting can stop for the primary system.

steps.title: 7. Verify Normal Startup Sequence
steps.instructions: Observe a controlled restart with no patient dependent on the system. Allow the system adequate time to initialize without repeatedly cycling power. Confirm that required mapping, acquisition, display, and workstation components become available. Expected outcome: Startup completes without repeated errors, freezes, or component-not-ready conditions.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before return to service, verify the system reaches its normal operational state and required external hardware is recognized. Confirm: Controls respond normally Displays are stable Required interfaces are available No unresolved startup alerts remain A basic nonpatient functional check is successful Expected outcome: The OPAL HDx is stable and ready for clinical setup. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Escalate an Unresolved Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If the system repeatedly fails startup despite verified power, connections, displays, and external accessories, stop external troubleshooting. Do not open internal assemblies or attempt board-level repair without appropriate authorization and manufacturer procedures. Expected outcome: The device is removed from clinical use and routed for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the OPAL HDx powered partially but would not complete startup before an electrophysiology procedure.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external system connection partially seated following equipment movement.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, restarted the system, verified normal initialization and component recognition, and completed a functional check before returning it to service.

title: Boston Scientific OPAL HDx Electrophysiology Mapping System - Workstation Freezes or Loses Communication
description: Troubleshoots frozen workstation operation or communication loss caused by external connections, network paths, peripherals, system state, or workstation instability.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Procedure Continuity
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a frozen or disconnected mapping workstation while the patient depends on it for procedural guidance. Notify the clinical team and maintain required independent monitoring. Avoid immediately rebooting if doing so could discard clinically important data. Expected outcome: Patient safety and necessary procedural information are protected before technical intervention.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Failure Type
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The entire workstation is frozen Mouse or keyboard input alone is unavailable Mapping acquisition continues but the display is unresponsive Communication with acquisition hardware is lost Network communication alone is lost The workstation spontaneously restarts Record any message and what functions remain operational. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to workstation responsiveness, peripheral input, hardware communication, or networking.

steps.title: 3. Check External Input Devices and Displays
steps.instructions: Inspect keyboard, mouse, display, and other accessible workstation peripherals. Verify they have normal power and connections. A failed peripheral can create the appearance of a frozen workstation. Expected outcome: External workstation controls and displays are functional. If replacing or reconnecting a peripheral restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Communication Cables
steps.instructions: Check accessible connections between the workstation and mapping/acquisition system components. Look for: Loose Ethernet or communication cables Damaged connectors Cables under tension Connections disturbed during equipment movement Reseat approved external connections. Expected outcome: Required communication connections are secure. If communication immediately returns and remains stable, troubleshooting can stop after testing.

steps.title: 5. Check Network Link Indications When Relevant
steps.instructions: If the lost communication depends on an Ethernet connection, inspect accessible link indicators and network connections. Determine whether the issue is: Workstation-to-system hardware Workstation-to-hospital network Both Do not change IP addressing, VLANs, security settings, or other network configuration without authorization. Expected outcome: The affected communication path is identified.

steps.title: 6. Determine Whether Data Must Be Preserved
steps.instructions: Before restarting the workstation, ask clinical staff whether an active or completed study contains information that has not been saved or exported. Follow approved shutdown or restart procedures whenever the workstation remains responsive enough to do so. Expected outcome: Clinically important data is protected as much as practical before restart.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Restart When Appropriate
steps.instructions: With no patient dependent on the system and after preserving available data, perform an approved workstation or system restart. Observe startup and reconnection of mapping hardware. Expected outcome: The workstation becomes responsive and reconnects normally. If communication remains stable through functional testing, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Verify Communication and Functional Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm: Required acquisition hardware is connected Workstation controls respond Displays update normally Test acquisition is stable Networked functions required for clinical use are available Expected outcome: Workstation and system communication remain stable during testing.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Repeated Freezes or Communication Loss
steps.instructions: If the workstation repeatedly freezes, restarts, or loses communication after external connections and peripherals are verified, remove the system from service. Do not perform unsupported software changes or internal computer repair while the system is designated for clinical use. Expected outcome: Recurrent instability is referred for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the OPAL HDx workstation lost communication with the mapping hardware during system setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external communication cable partially disconnected at the workstation.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the connection, restarted the system in a controlled manner, and verified stable hardware communication and test acquisition.
